title: Compliance export rules engine for granular retention and region-aware shipping
creator: Nathan Chen
description:
Problem: Customers operating in regulated regions need a single, auditable export pipeline that enforces per-tenant retention policies, respects data residency rules, and delivers scheduled or on-demand artifacts (PDF/CSV) with cryptographic proof of provenance. Current exports are piecemeal and rely on ad-hoc scripts.

Goal: Ship a rules-driven export engine that: 1) evaluates tenant-level retention & residency policies at time of export, 2) can transform and paginate exports into PDF and CSV with configurable schemas, 3) attaches a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums + signing key id) for each export, 4) supports delivery channels (S3 presigned URL, encrypted email, SFTP, webhook) and schedule definitions (cron-like recurrence and TTL), and 5) surfaces export status and lineage in Console and via API.

Scope: The work in this ticket covers API and backend orchestration (rules evaluation, export generation worker, signing and packaging), Console UX for export rule authoring and schedule management, RBAC checks, integration with KMS for signing/encryption, and audit log entries for every export lifecycle event. It excludes long-term archival storage (handled by a follow-up), bulk CSV normalization libraries (can use existing util), and migration of legacy ad-hoc export jobs (handled by migration plan).

Acceptance criteria: 
- New REST endpoints: POST /v1/exports/rules (author rule), GET /v1/exports/{id}/status, POST /v1/exports/{id}/run-now
- Exports must enforce tenant residency (region filter) and retention cutoff before materializing any records
- Output formats: PDF with table-of-contents and CSV with schema mapping; both compressed into a single .zip with manifest.json.gz containing checksums and a signer metadata object
- Manifest must be signed with customer or platform KMS key (configurable) and verifiable via public key artifact in Console
- Scheduled exports must be creatable in Console with recurrence window and per-run TTL; runs must be queued and visible in export history
- Audit trail entries for rule changes, runs, delivery attempts and failures
- Unit and integration tests covering rules evaluation and signing logic

Non-functional requirements: 
- Export generation must parallelize per-tenant shards to meet 99th percentile SLA of 3 minutes for exports under 10k records
- Jobs should be idempotent and resume from checkpoint after worker restarts
- Sensitive fields must be redacted according to tenant redaction policy when requested

Design docs and artifacts: 
- Internal design doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/pm/compliance-exports-rules-engine (draft)
- Prototype Console mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/placeholder (see mock_v2_authoring.png)
- Runtime perf tests: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/exports/perf

Rollout plan (high-level): create opt-in beta for 3 pilot tenants -> collect perf and correctness metrics -> enable for customers with compliance_contract flag -> GA. Rollback: toggle feature flag and cancel queued runs; previous ad-hoc exports remain available during transition.
comments: 2025-01-29 - Asha Patel: Created initial PRD and prioritized in cycle 2025-W06. Linked design doc and mocks.

2025-02-03 - Miguel Rivera (ENG): Spike completed for signing + manifest format. Found trade-off between embedding full signer certificate vs pointer to KMS key; recommending pointer to reduce payload size. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
2025-02-06 - Priya Shah (SEC): Requested threat model for signing key rotation and export replay protection. Added to security review checklist.
2025-02-10 - Asha Patel: UX review notes - add confirmation modal for schedule creation and preview of example PDF header. Updated mocks in Drive.

2025-02-12 - Nathan Chen (PM): Backend implementation started. Worker uses job shards keyed by tenant-region. First integration smoke test: export of 2k records succeeded (end-to-end). CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/export-rules/125
2025-02-14 - QA (Elena Morris): Found edge case where retention cutoff == export timestamp causing off-by-one exclusion. Filing follow-up ENG ticket ENG-8539 to fix timezone normalization.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: two signing modes (platform-sign vs customer-managed keys). Started with platform-sign with an operator option to enable customer-managed KMS per contract.
Delivery channels prioritized: S3 presigned -> webhook -> SFTP -> email. Email delivery will be encrypted and limited to compliance contacts only.
We will expose a verification endpoint /v1/exports/verify-manifest that accepts a manifest and returns verification status for auditors.
Follow-ups: archival lifecycle connector (PM-XXXXX), streaming export for >1M records (separate project), migration plan to convert legacy ad-hoc jobs to rules engine.
